steps.title: Slide across
steps.text: A pan is when the camera slides sideways, like turning your head to look across a room. Everything in the picture slides the other way. Start and stop gently (ease in and ease out) so it's not jerky.

steps.title: Long backgrounds
steps.text: For a pan, draw a background much wider than the screen, then slide it a little each frame. The orange box is what the camera sees.

steps.title: Pan past a tree
steps.text: The camera pans right, so the tree slides left. Ease in and out: small, big, small gaps.
steps.hint: Small gap, big gap, small gap.

quiz.question: When the camera pans right, the background moves...
quiz.explain: The camera moves one way, so the picture slides the other way.

lessons.title: Parallax
lessons.summary: Near is fast, far is slow.

steps.title: Near is fast, far is slow
steps.text: When the camera moves sideways, things close to it zoom past while far things barely move. This is parallax, and it makes a flat drawing feel deep. Here the fence moves 4 times as fast as the mountains, and the trees twice as fast.

steps.title: Parallax with layers
steps.text: Put each depth on its own layer.

tasks: Draw the mountains on a Back layer, trees on a Middle layer, and a fence on a Front layer.
On each new frame, move the Front layer a lot, the Middle a little, and the Back just a tiny bit.
Play it back. Does it feel deep?

quiz.question: Which layer moves fastest in a parallax shot?
choices: The one closest to the camera
quiz.explain: Near things cross your view quickly; far things take ages.

quiz.question: The fence moves 4 steps each frame and the trees move 2. How far should the far mountains move?
quiz.explain: Further away means slower, so the mountains move the least.

lessons.title: Orbit
lessons.summary: Circle the camera around the subject.

steps.title: Circling around
steps.text: In an orbit, the camera circles around the subject. Things in front of the subject slide one way, and things behind it slide the other way. It's tricky to draw by hand, so keep shapes simple: boxes and cylinders on a ground grid.

steps.title: Orbit a box
steps.text: Draw the box as the camera moves around it.
steps.hint: The front corner moves across a little each frame.

quiz.question: When the camera orbits around a statue, things behind the statue...
choices: Slide the opposite way to things in front
quiz.explain: The camera swings around the middle, so front and back move in opposite directions.

steps.title: Zoom vs push in
steps.text: A zoom makes everything bigger together, like a magnifying glass. A push in moves the camera closer: the near box grows fast while the far box hardly changes. A push in feels like walking into the scene.

steps.title: Zoom in on the sun
steps.text: Draw the sun getting bigger on each frame, staying in the middle.
steps.hint: The middle stays put; everything grows outward.

quiz.question: In a push in, which things get bigger fastest?
quiz.explain: Moving closer changes near things a lot and far things only a little.
